verifications.claim: NHL playoff overtime consists of 20-minute 5-on-5 sudden-death periods
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "teams will play a 20-minute, sudden-death overtime period... Overtime in the Stanley Cup Playoffs is played as 5-on-5" (R1); "20-minute periods of 5-on-5 hockey until one side scores" (R2); "Overtime periods last 20 minutes... It's five-on-five play (barring penalties)" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state 20-minute 5-on-5 sudden-death periods in playoffs.

verifications.claim: NHL playoff overtime periods are repeated until a winner is decided
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "More overtime periods will be added until either team scores a winning goal" (R1); "play 20-minute periods of 5-on-5 hockey until one side scores" (R2); "If no one scores in the first overtime, the process repeats and continues until someone scores" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources confirm periods continue until a goal is scored.

verifications.claim: There are no shootouts in NHL playoff overtime unlike the regular season
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "There are no shootouts in playoff hockey" (R1); "There are no shootouts in the playoffs" (R2); "no more shootouts after five minutes of scoreless play, as happens during regular-season overtime" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly contrast playoffs (no shootouts) with regular season (shootouts).

verifications.claim: There is no 3-on-3 play in NHL playoff overtime unlike the regular season
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "In the playoffs, there is no three-on-three" (cited snippet, R7); "Overtime in the Stanley Cup Playoffs is played as 5-on-5" vs. "NHL overtime is played 3-on-3" regular (R1); "No more three-on-three play" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Direct statements confirm no 3-on-3 in playoffs, contrasting regular season.

verifications.claim: Intermissions between NHL playoff overtime periods are 15 minutes
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "the teams go to the dressing rooms for 15 minutes" (R3); "Full 20-minute periods with 15-minute intermissions between them" (R5); "the game will pause for 15 minutes" (R7)

verifications.claim: The ice is resurfaced during intermissions between NHL playoff overtime periods
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Players go to the dressing room while the ice is resurfaced" (R3); "teams return to their dressing rooms and the ice is resurfaced" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly mention ice resurfacing during intermissions.

verifications.claim: All NHL playoff overtime goals are reviewed by officials
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The NHL Situation Room reviews all goals to make sure they are legally scored" (R3); "All overtime goals are reviewed by NHL officials" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Direct statements confirm all OT goals are reviewed.

verifications.claim: In NHL playoff overtime, the first team to score wins
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "sudden-death overtime period until a winner is determined" (R1); "the first team to score wins the game instantly" (R2); "Yes, it's sudden death. Once a team scores... the game is over" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Sudden-death format clearly means first goal wins.

verifications.claim: If a NHL playoff overtime period ends without a goal, another 20-minute period is played
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "If there is no winner after the initial 20 minutes, they'll go to a second overtime period" (R1); "If no one scores after 20 minutes in the first overtime... they play a second overtime" (R3)

verifications.claim: Penalties carry over from regulation and between NHL playoff overtime periods
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Penalties in overtime during the postseason would be treated as they would be during regulation" (R1); "Remaining time from a penalty assessed near or at the end of regulation — or from the previous overtime period — carries over" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm penalties carry over from regulation and prior OT periods.

verifications.claim: In NHL playoff overtime, 3-on-3 or 4-on-4 may occur if penalties are served
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: "five-on-five play (barring penalties)" (R3); "Penalties result in a player to the penalty box for the offending team and a power play" (R5); "barring penalties" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Sources indicate manpower changes due to penalties (power plays, e.g., 5-4 or 4-4 possible), but do not specify 3-on-3 or 4-on-4 explicitly; broader description supports possibility indirectly.

verifications.claim: The default in NHL playoff overtime is 5-on-5
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Overtime in the Stanley Cup Playoffs is played as 5-on-5" (R1); "5-on-5 hockey" (R2); "It's five-on-five play (barring penalties)" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: All sources directly state default is 5-on-5.
